hints: Look closely at where the dark chromosomes are in each photo: tangled in a ball, scattered, lined up in the middle, pulled apart, or in two separate clumps.
Remember the mitosis story in order: chromosomes condense in prophase, line up on the equator in metaphase, sister chromatids separate in anaphase, then two new nuclei form in telophase.
walkthrough:
**Identify the start and the middle**

First, find prophase and metaphase. Photo 2 shows a tangled ball of condensing chromosomes filling the nucleus, so that is early prophase. Photo 5 shows chromosomes lined up in a neat single row across the middle, so that is metaphase.

Remember: prophase comes first, metaphase comes in the middle.

**Place the in-between and the separation stages**

Photo 3 shows individual thick chromosomes scattered around the cell, with the nuclear envelope gone. That is late prophase (prometaphase), just after photo 2 and just before lining up. Photo 1 shows two V-shaped sets of chromatids being pulled to opposite poles. That is anaphase, just after metaphase.

**Spot the finish and put it all together**

Photo 4 shows two small, tight clumps of chromosomes far apart at opposite ends of the cell. That is telophase, the last stage when two daughter nuclei start to form.

So the story runs:
$$2 (early prophase) \rightarrow 3 (late prophase) \rightarrow 5 (metaphase) \rightarrow 1 (anaphase) \rightarrow 4 (telophase)$$

options.A: Correct. This gives the true biological sequence from chromosome condensation to two separate nuclei: 2 to 3 to 5 to 1 to 4.
options.B: False. This puts telophase (4) second and metaphase (5) fourth, which is backwards because lining up must happen before separation and formation of two nuclei.
options.C: False. This starts with scattered chromosomes (3) before the tangled condensing mass (2), but condensation in early prophase must come first.
options.D: False. This starts with metaphase (5) and ends with prophase (2), which reverses mitosis because prophase is the start, not the end.
